# Template: anatomy
The human body drawn from a named anatomical atlas, seen from the front: a body outline with the internal organs (default) and/or the skeleton with its joints, coloured by part, at three levels of detail. EVERY DRAWN PART IS A NAMED ELEMENT whose id is the part's own name (heart, liver, femur_left, knee_left), so `ask` with widget "click" and answer "liver" asks the viewer to find the liver on the body, and `quiz` can ask about any of them. `detail` 1 shows the big organs and a coarse skeleton of 17 regions (skull, spine, rib_cage, pelvis, hand_left…); 2 (the default) the named bones, joints and smaller organs; 3 the small bones of hands and feet and the fine organs — the ids CHANGE with the level (hand_left at 1–2, its carpals_left / metacarpals_left / phalanges_hand_left at 3), so name the ids of the level you chose. `focus` narrows to one part and its children at full detail — the way to zoom in on the abdomen, the left hand, or the knee; the `highlight` PARAM tints parts for the whole figure — to make a part glow for ONE sentence use the highlight COMMAND ({"highlight": {"target": ["liver"]}, "speak": "…"}), and a click question glows its answer part by itself when the answer is spoken; `markers` drops labelled dots; `findings` puts DISEASE into a part for the viewer to identify; `names` chooses the label language. Choose this scene for ANY request to draw, label, locate or quiz the human body, an organ, a bone, a joint, the skeleton, the abdomen, or where something is in the body. An unrecognised part name is skipped and listed in a small note rather than failing. The ⬡ 3D button in the app shows the same body as meshes — say so in a closing line when the lesson is about shape or depth. Silhouettes are frontal projections of BodyParts3D meshes (© The Database Center for Life Science, CC BY-SA 2.1 Japan).

Element ids your commands can reference:
- body_outline: the body's silhouette — a skin wash by default (outline: skin), an ink outline (line), or absent (none); under focus only a clipped wash, never a stroke
- frame: a light dashed frame around the crop, present only under focus
- <part_id>: every drawn part is its own element and its id IS its anatomical id (heart, liver, femur_left, knee_left, hand_left at detail 1–2, carpals_left at detail 3) — these are the ids an ask with widget "click" compares against
- label_<part_id>: that part's written name, when labels ask for it
- marker_<i> / marker_label_<i>: markers[i] and its caption
- finding_<part_id> / label_finding_<part_id>: the abnormality drawn into that part, and its caption when given
- missing_note: "Unknown: …" for names that matched nothing, and "Detail reduced" when the request was too dense to draw
- title: figure title, when set
Examples:
Request: "Draw the organs of the human body and label them." → params: {"labels":"all","detail":1}
Request: "Where is the liver? Show the body so I can point at it." → params: {"systems":["viscera"],"detail":2,"highlight":["liver"],"labels":"none"}
Request: "Vis hva som ligger bak tarmene." → params: {"systems":["viscera"],"detail":2,"layer":"deep","labels":"all","names":"nb"}
Request: "The skeleton in plain ink, with the knees marked." → params: {"systems":["skeleton"],"detail":2,"color":"mono","outline":"line","highlight":["knee_left","knee_right"],"labels":"focus"}

In YAML: `template: anatomy` and `params:` per the schema above; commands name the element ids above.
